practices.practice: Create a single, process-wide MongoClient and reuse it (singleton); tune connection-pool parameters (maxPoolSize/minPoolSize/maxIdleTimeMS) appropriate to the deployment rather than creating a new client per request.
practices.prior_belief: Use a pooled MongoClient with explicit maxPoolSize and socketTimeoutMS settings (configure connection pool sizing appropriate for expected concurrency, e.g., maxPoolSize=50) rather than opening/closing a new client per request.

practices.practice: Always require TLS on the MongoDB driver connection and validate server certificates in production (do not disable certificate validation in production environments).
practices.prior_belief: Enable TLS/SSL on the MongoDB driver connection and validate server certificates (e.g., tls=true/ssl=true and tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false) to encrypt traffic to the DocumentDB cluster.

practices.practice: Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and never embed credentials in code, committed config files, or logs.
practices.prior_belief: Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never embed credentials in code, config files committed to the repo, or printed to logs.

practices.practice: Run server-side aggregation pipelines (aggregate) to compute metrics like seasonal sales velocity rather than pulling raw documents into the application for client-side computation.
practices.prior_belief: Use server-side aggregation pipelines (MongoDB aggregate) rather than pulling raw documents into the app and computing metrics client-side to reduce network transfer and leverage DB compute.

practices.practice: Push $match and $project stages to the start of aggregation pipelines (filter by date range and category first, then project needed fields) to minimize scanned documents and I/O.
practices.prior_belief: When queries compute seasonal sales velocity, push $match and $project to the start of the aggregation pipeline (filter by date range and category first, then project only needed fields) to minimize processed data.

practices.practice: Before adding or changing indexes, run explain("executionStats") or use the MCP explain_operation to verify the query/aggregation plan, index usage, and keys/docs examined.
practices.prior_belief: Before adding or changing indexes, run explain() or use the MCP server tools to verify the aggregation/query plan uses the intended index and to measure I/O and RU/ops cost.

practices.practice: Design compound indexes following ESR (Equality → Sort → Range); for seasonal aggregations create a compound index such as {category: 1, sale_date: 1} to cover common $match and $sort patterns.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes that support the aggregation pipeline: add an index on {category:1, date:1} (or {season:1, category:1, date:1} if season is queried frequently) so $match/$sort stages are covered and the pipeline can be executed efficiently.

practices.practice: Make seeding idempotent by using unique keys (e.g., tx_id) and upsert semantics (update_one with upsert or bulk upsert/$setOnInsert) so repeated runs do not create duplicates.
practices.prior_belief: Seed data idempotently using upsert or bulkWrite with ordered=false so repeated runs do not create duplicates and are efficient (use a unique sales_id key and bulk operations for large loads).

practices.practice: Handle transient network and server errors with retries and exponential backoff; enable driver retryReads/retryWrites for retryable operations and implement application-level retries only for idempotent operations.
practices.prior_belief: Handle transient network and server errors with retries using exponential backoff, and distinguish idempotent vs non-idempotent operations (retry only idempotent reads/aggregation; for writes use upsert or ensure idempotency tokens).

practices.practice: Shard only when needed; choose a shard key that matches workload patterns—high-cardinality evenly-distributed keys for write-heavy workloads and the most-frequently-used query filter for read-heavy workloads; avoid low-cardinality fields like season as a shard key.
practices.prior_belief: Choose a high-cardinality, immutable partition key for the collection to avoid hot partitions (for example a store_id or region_id rather than a low-cardinality season field) and design documents so the chosen key is present and stable.

practices.practice: For vector-capable clusters, create vector indexes with the appropriate engine and parameters (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF; set dimensions, similarity metric, lBuild, lSearch, maxDegree) before running k-NN queries.
practices.prior_belief: For the vector-capable cluster, ensure vector fields have an index created with appropriate algorithm and parameters (e.g., HNSW or IVF options such as M/efConstruction or nlist) and that the index dimension and metric match the stored vectors before running k-NN queries.

practices.practice: Keep vector dimensionality consistent across all documents, normalize embeddings when using cosine similarity, and validate vector length at insert time to avoid index or query errors.
practices.prior_belief: Keep vector dimensionality consistent across all documents, and store vectors in a typed array or fixed-length list field; validate vector length at insert time to avoid index/query failures.

practices.practice: Tune vector query-time parameters (e.g., lSearch / ef/runtime and k) to balance recall vs latency and record those settings alongside the index configuration.
practices.prior_belief: When performing approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) queries, tune query-time parameters (e.g., ef/runtime search size) to balance recall vs latency and record those settings as part of the tool configuration.

practices.practice: Use createSearchIndexes and the $search aggregation stage for full-text search; prefer DocumentDB's search tooling over community $text and build custom analyzers for case-insensitive, prefix, or hierarchical matching as needed.
Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logging, send them to Log Analytics, and create alerts on CPU/memory/IOPS/storage/connection saturation to detect and diagnose performance issues.
practices.prior_belief: Log operations, query parameters, pipeline shapes, and costs (RU/latency) but scrub or redact any secrets; keep sufficient telemetry to diagnose slow aggregations or index misses.

practices.practice: Limit credentials to least privilege: prefer Microsoft Entra ID + RBAC and create per-application roles/users with only the permissions required (e.g., read-only user for analytic agents).
practices.prior_belief: Limit database credentials to least privilege required (create a database user with only read on the sales collection for the agent's analysis tool; separate a different key/user for administrative seeding tasks).

practices.practice: Provision throughput by choosing the appropriate cluster compute tier and storage (Premium SSD v2) because IOPS and bandwidth are gated by compute tier rather than by RU/s or disk size; size compute for expected aggregation workloads.
practices.prior_belief: Provision sufficient throughput (RU/s or appropriate cluster tier) for expected aggregation workloads and enable autoscale where available to handle spikes from periodic batch aggregation or agent runs.

practices.practice: Minimize the fields returned by queries using projection and paginate results (prefer range-based cursors where possible) to reduce memory usage, network transfer, and query cost.
practices.prior_belief: Minimize the fields returned by queries (use projection) and paginate with range-based cursors where possible to avoid large in-memory result sets and to reduce RU/latency.

practices.practice: For local development, use the DocumentDB Gateway Docker image (Mongo on port 10260), drive TLS relaxation from environment variables, and keep connection abstractions consistent with production.

Do not assume Azure DocumentDB uses Cosmos DB RU/s autoscale semantics; consult DocumentDB docs for backup/HA timelines and use HA (in-region) and cross-region replicas for higher SLAs and resilience.

When adding or changing search/indexing for full-text or hybrid retrieval, use the documented createSearchIndexes command and target $search by index name; hybrid BM25+vector retrieval is supported via application-side fusion.

Before large index changes or drops, follow a safe lifecycle: inventory existing indexes, hide the index to validate impact, then drop if unused, because index count and maintenance have a write cost.
Use product-managed backups and enable HA for production clusters; DocumentDB provides continuous automatic backups (35 days for active clusters) and HA for zone/node failover.

Normalize and record vector metadata (model name and dimensionality) alongside vectors and consider product quantization or fp16 indexing to reduce memory footprint when using high-dimensional vectors.
When building a production topology, enable availability-zone in-region HA for the 99.99% SLA and add cross-region replicas (follow the post-promotion runbook) if you need the 99.995% SLA.
Before running vector k-NN queries, combine pre-filters (e.g., category/date range) with the vector search to reduce the candidate set and improve latency and recall.
When running heavy ingestion or large seeding jobs, monitor for throttling and back off if the cluster signals rate limiting; prefer batching but validate batch size against observed throttling.

Prefer the Gateway for local development with pinned docker-compose, expose only required ports (10260 for Mongo), and keep local TLS relaxation under environment control (do not bake tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=true into code).
Enable and use MCP/mongosh explain, list_indexes and indexStats workflows as part of routine query tuning and index lifecycle management.

Do not assume Cross-product docs (MongoDB, Cosmos DB, Amazon DocumentDB) are authoritative for Azure DocumentDB; check DocumentDB-specific docs for index types, search commands (createSearchIndexes), and vector index engines.
Application-level external search calls (e.g., Bing) should use timeouts, retries, and fallbacks, but this is not specified in Azure DocumentDB docs (application concern).
practices.prior_belief: Use timeouts on external web-search requests and a deterministic fallback (mock) so the LangChain agent remains responsive if the search API is slow or unavailable; apply retries/timeouts and circuit breaker patterns.

practices.practice: Batch large seed ingestion carefully (monitor for throttling) — the public DocumentDB guidance documents monitoring and throttling behaviors but do not mandate a specific batch size like 1k–10k; choose batch size based on observed throttling and metrics.
practices.prior_belief: When seeding large datasets, use bulkWrite in batches (e.g., 1k–10k docs per batch) and monitor for rate limiting or RU exhaustion; slow down or back off if you see throughput throttling errors.

practices.practice: Storing temporal fields in UTC using BSON Date objects and designing seasonal comparisons with explicit date ranges is good practice in applications, but DocumentDB docs do not contain an Azure-specific mandate beyond using date types for index friendliness.
practices.prior_belief: Store temporal fields in UTC using BSON Date objects and design seasonal comparisons with explicit date ranges (avoid storing local-time strings) so aggregations on date arithmetic are correct and index-friendly.
